title: Transactional microframes + client telemetry playbook (PRD draft)
content:
Context and problem statement:

We keep getting production reports about user-facing failures during long-running multi-tool interactions: partial outputs are lost, retries cause duplicate tool calls, and engineers have limited visibility into which micro-step caused the regression. Existing streaming partials are too coarse (full chunk or whole-tool) and client SDKs surface only raw events, leaving integration teams to implement brittle reconciliation logic.

Objective (what success looks like):
- Define a compact, transactional framing for streaming responses that lets the server declare micro-steps (microframes) with commit/abort semantics for tool calls and structured output segments.
- Make the client-side SDK ergonomic so app teams get at-most-once tool semantics by default, simple resumability, and built-in telemetry for debugging/quality metrics.
- Provide fallback behaviors and an ops-visible event model so SREs can route degraded requests to cheaper/compatible models without breaking tool transactions.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not propose changes to the wire protocol used by Dedicated/Private control planes today. Focus is hosted API SDK + server-side framing.
- Not attempting to solve application-level idempotency beyond providing the primitives (transaction ids, sequence ids).

Design principles:
- Minimal surface area: only a few new frame types added to streaming (MICROFRAME_BEGIN, MICROFRAME_END, TOOL_COMMIT, TOOL_ABORT, CHECKPOINT).
- Explicit transaction ids: every microframe group carries a transaction_id (short base62) that is stable across retries and resumptions.
- Small frames: microframes contain compact metadata and optional small JSON payloads for structured output. Large blobs still stream as chunks.

Microframe lifecycle (example):
1) MICROFRAME_BEGIN {transaction_id: t1, type: "tool-call", step: 1}
2) streaming content tokens for user-visible text or partial structured JSON
3) TOOL_COMMIT {transaction_id: t1, tool_instance: "send-email:v3", result_ref: "r-7f2"}
OR TOOL_ABORT {transaction_id: t1, reason: "timeout"}
4) CHECKPOINT {transaction_id: t1, cursor: 45678} (optional; server-suggested prefix cache key)

Semantic guarantees: 
- At-most-once tool semantics by default: server will not emit TOOL_COMMIT more than once per transaction_id (unless a resumed duplicate occurs; client SDK deduplicates by commit id).
- Resumability: if a client reconnects and presents last_seen_cursor + transaction_ids, server will replay incomplete transactions with a RESUME_HINT frame: client can safely continue or request abort.

SDK ergonomics (JS/TS + Python):
- High-level primitive: session.transaction({type: 'tool', id: t1}, async (ctx) => { await ctx.callTool('send-email', payload) })
  - SDK handles attaching transaction_id to frames, retry coordination, and local commit de-dup table.
  - Default config: 30s tool call acknowledgement timeout; configurable per-call.
- Low-level primitive: stream.on('microframe', handler) exposing raw frames for advanced use.
- Telemetry hooks: client emits event telemetry (microframe.sent, microframe.committed, microframe.aborted, resume.attempt) to Redwood console via anonymized ids. Ops can correlate to server traces.

Observability and SLOs:
- Per-transaction metrics: p95 time-to-commit, commit/failure-rate by model & tool, resumed-transaction-rate.
- Alert rule examples: commit-failure-rate > 0.5% for 5m on production model => page.
- Correlation fields: transaction_id, request_id, model_variant, region, client_sdk_version.

Fallback & graceful degradation policy:
- If a high-performance model can’t handle tool-call semantics under load, smart routing will fallback to a compatible model variant that supports microframes but may have higher latency. Server emits FALLBACK_NOTICE frame with reason and new model id.
- SDK default behavior: if FALLBACK_NOTICE arrives mid-transaction, SDK emits a telemetry marker and continues; application-level behavior controlled via callback.

Security and safety notes:
- Tool identifiers and result_refs must not leak PII; server will sanitize result metadata in public frames. Full tool payloads always delivered on TLS channels and only to authenticated clients.
- Transaction ids rotating per session to limit long-term correlation.

Rollout plan (staged):
- Alpha: internal-only SDK + server flags (2 weeks) — integrations with Solutions Eng on one live customer scenario.
- Beta: opt-in tenant flag for hosted API + public SDK patch (4 weeks) — collect telemetry, iterate on dedupe heuristics.
- GA: default on for new client versions; clear migration guide for older clients (8 weeks)

Metrics to validate success (90-day window):
- Reduced duplicated tool executions by >=75% for beta tenants.
- Reduced visible user regressions tied to partial-loss by >=60%.
- Adoption: >=40% of top-20 integrators on SDK vX within 60 days of GA.

Open questions / risks:
- How does this interact with third-party tool idempotency? (need SRE + legal input)
- Server storage overhead for resumability cursors at scale — we may need TTL strategies.
- UX for developers who don't want transactional semantics (must remain zero-config opt-out).

Next steps / short-term action items:
- Product: finalize frame names & small JSON schema (Aisha) — due 2025-02-22.
- Eng (serving-runtime): prototype microframe emitter and commit dedupe store; demo with send-email tool (Marco) — spike by 2025-02-28.
- DX/SDK: implement high-level session.transaction API in JS SDK + example app and migration guide (Lena) — first pass by 2025-03-07.
- SRE: propose TTL and scaling plan for resumability cursors (Samir) — 2025-03-05.

Notes to self / rough brainstorming fragments:
- could use short-lived signed commit tokens to prove commit ownership in multi-client flows.
- consider wire-compact encoding for microframe headers to save bytes for small messages.
- encourage integrators to keep tool calls idempotent even with server guarantees.

Appendix: example event trace (compact):
- request_id: r-5423, transaction_id: t1, frames: [MICROFRAME_BEGIN->tokens->TOOL_COMMIT(result_ref=r-7f2)->CHECKPOINT]

End of draft.
